expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: "Between the migration running and your last old pod draining, old code is selecting a column that no longer exists — those three call sites throw for real users."

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: "Today — ship only the code change... Next week — after the old version is out of rotation... ship the DROP alone."

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: "Nothing restores it in place. Your only recovery is a point-in-time restore of the whole database to before the migration."

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: "Step one reverts in minutes... Step two has no rollback at all, so it wants a Tuesday morning and someone watching."

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: "Step two has no rollback at all, so it wants a Tuesday morning and someone watching."

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: "a CI check that blocks DROP/destructive ALTER from landing in the same diff as application code."

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: "Short answer: merge the code change, hold the DROP."

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: "Expand → backfill → dual-write → switch reads are all reversible; only contract isn't."
